children: Renewable energy stocks such as Suzlon Energy, Premier Energies, Waaree Energiesplunged in trade, dragged by their peers Inox Wind and Vikram Solar, who are reacting to their second quarter results on Monday, November 16.
Both, Inox Wind and Vikram Solar reported weak earnings in the September quarter over the weekend, while the other three companies delivered mixed results.
Why Inox Wind Fell On Monday?
Inox Wind's net profit fell 35.9% to ₹58.83 crore from ₹91.75 crore, even as its revenue rose 21% to ₹1,354.3 crore from ₹1,119 crore last year.

Its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) fell 10.1% to ₹205 crore from ₹228 crore and its EBITDA margin missed Street estimates and also contracted to 15.2% from 20.4% from the year-ago period.
The company's margins were impacted by higher commodity prices.
Inox Wind shares declined 9.99% in intraday trade, its biggest single-day loss since May 28, 2024, when it had fallen just as much. The stock is now 60% below its 52-week high.
Vikram Solar Reacts To Results
Vikram Solar's earnings declined across all key parameters in the second quarter.
Its profit after tax (PAT) plunged 95% to ₹5.9 crore from ₹128 crore in the second quarter last fiscal. Its revenue was down 2.9% at ₹1,077 crore from ₹1,110 crore in the previous year.
The company's EBITDA also fell 57% to ₹101 crore from ₹235 crore and its margins contracted sharply to 9.3% from 21.1% in the year-ago period.
Sales volume for the quarter fell to 591 mega watt (MW) from 1,006 MW in the prior quarter. The same was also down 25% from the previous year.

However, Vikram Solar, in its investor presentation said the headwinds in the September quarter were transitory as monsoon and deferred execution impacted results. India installations also declined 25%.

The company said its first cell will be out in December 2026. The cost base also had an impact as modules till now are being built on bought-in cells till the company's own cell plant begins. This, with competitive pressure in the non-DCR modules impacted its results.
Vikram Solar shares fell nearly 9% in intraday trade.
Impact on peers
Taking cue, shares of Suzlon Energy, Premier Energies and Waaree Energies fell up to 7% in intraday trade on Monday.
Suzlon Energy

shares extended their losses for the fifth consecutive session, falling 3.5% to hit an intraday low of ₹36.93 apiece on Monday. The stock was down 2.9% at ₹37.13 apiece. It has declined 11.6% in the past month and 30.3% in the last six months.

Suzlon Energy, which reported its second quarter earnings at the end of October, received multiple price cuts on its stock after the company's management revised its full-year EBITDA margin guidance down to 15% plus-minus, from the previous one of 17% plus-minus.

In the second quarter, its margin had contracted to 21.2% from 26.9% in the year-ago period because of non-recurring opex (100 basis points), consumer or scope mix (150-180 basis points) and forex and commodity volatility (50 basis points).
Meanwhile,
Premier Energies

shares snapped their two-day gain by falling 7.1% to hit an intraday low of ₹832.1 apiece on Monday. The stock has fallen 7.6% in the past month, 15.6% in the last six months and 1.8% in 2026, so far.

Last week, Premier Energies told CNBC-TV18 that it expects a strong growth over the next few years, supported by a healthy order book of about 16,600 crore and a near three-fold rise in business scale post its recent capacity expansions.

In the second quarter, its consolidated net profit was up 30% at ₹458 crore, revenue rose 43.3% to ₹2,632 crore from the previous year. Its EBITDA increased 31.2% to ₹736 crore but its EBITDA margin contracted to 28% from 30.5% in the previous year.
Lastly, shares of
Waaree Energies
extended loses for the second day, falling 4.4% to hit an intraday low of ₹2,435 apiece. The stock has declined 4.8% in the last month and 18.6% in the last six months.

The company reported its earnings for the second quarter last month. Its consolidated net profit was down 214.7% at ₹718.68 crore, while its revenue increased 23.9% to ₹7,518 crore from ₹6,066 crore last year. Its EBITDA fell 5% to ₹1,336 crore and its EBITDA margin contracted to 18% from 23%.

title: Suzlon Energy, Premier, Waaree shares fall up to 7% after peers report disappointing Q2 results
